title: Samples nyctaxi Use Cases Catalog
executive_summary:
Samples nyctaxi operates in one of the most data-rich environments in urban mobility, where every trip generates signals about fares, demand, duration, and revenue that can be turned into decisive commercial advantage. This catalog charts a clear path for Samples nyctaxi to convert that raw trip-level data into margin, service quality, and growth through the strategic use of AI and Databricks Genie Code.

Concrete opportunities already stand out. Predict Trip Fares to Grow Revenue enables upfront fare quotes grounded in predicted fare_amount to lift booked-trip conversion, while Forecast Trip Demand to Reduce Idle Cost repositions vehicles each shift to raise served-trip volume and cut idle time. On the integrity side, Detect Fare Irregularities to Protect Revenue gives revenue assurance teams a daily queue of flagged trips to recover under-billed fares. Together these show how predictive and generative AI move Samples nyctaxi from reactive reporting to proactive, revenue-shaping decisions.

Databricks Genie Code is the accelerant that makes this practical, letting analysts and operators interrogate trip data in natural language, build models faster, and operationalize insights without heavy engineering overhead. The result is a durable competitive edge: smarter pricing, leaner fleet operations, protected revenue, and sustained top-line growth.
domains_summary: Pricing: 4 use cases, Fleet: 3 use cases, Risk: 2 use cases, Revenue: 3 use cases

domains.summary:
Pricing is the primary lever through which Samples nyctaxi converts demand into profitable revenue, and it demands precision at the level of individual trips and zones. The domain is responsible for setting fare postures that balance competitiveness with margin, ensuring every corridor and segment earns its full potential.

Predict Trip Fares to Grow Revenue lets the Product Pricing Manager launch upfront fare quotes grounded in predicted fare_amount, increasing booked-trip conversion and customer trust. Segment Pickup Zones to Improve Margins assigns a differentiated pricing posture per zone segment to raise average fare_amount, while Identify Low-yield Trips to Protect Margins helps the Yield Management Analyst target corridors generating recurring low-yield trips and lift effective fare-per-trip. With Databricks Genie Code, these pricing models can be built, tested, and refined rapidly, turning pricing into a continuously optimized, data-driven discipline.

use_cases.Name: Predict Trip Fare from Route and Timing with Upfront Pricing Recommendations
use_cases.usecase: Predict Trip Fares to Grow Revenue
use_cases.Statement: Offering reliable upfront fares requires predicting `fare_amount` from route and timing before the trip completes, yet pricing currently depends on post-trip meter totals that cannot support quote-based products. This limits revenue from fixed-price offerings.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers features from `trip_distance`, `pickup_zip`, `dropoff_zip` and time-of-day/day-of-week derived from `tpep_pickup_datetime`, trains a Ridge regression (alpha tuned by cross-validation) to predict `fare_amount`, then uses ai_query to translate predicted fares into upfront quote recommendations.
use_cases.Business Value: The Product Pricing Manager launches upfront fare quotes grounded in predicted `fare_amount`, aiming to increase booked-trip conversion and protect realized fare-per-mile [ESTIMATE: depends on `fare_amount`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: fare_amount, trip_distance, pickup_zip, dropoff_zip, tpep_pickup_datetime. Engineer distance, corridor and hour/day-of-week features, train a Ridge regression to predict fare_amount with cross-validated alpha, evaluate residuals, then use ai_query to convert predictions into upfront pricing recommendations.
use_cases.Strategic Goals Alignment: Enable Data-Driven Decisions, Increase Revenue, Improve Customer Experience
use_cases.Justification: A fare prediction model enables upfront quote products, a direct revenue opportunity, with the target fare_amount and all predictors present; conversion lift moves a revenue line.
use_cases.Quality Summary: Predictors `trip_distance`, `pickup_zip`, `dropoff_zip` and time-of-day/day-of-week from `tpep_pickup_datetime` train a cross-validated Ridge regression to estimate `fare_amount` before trip completion, producing a predicted_fare per route-time with residual evaluation. ai_query converts predictions into upfront quote recommendations, enabling the fixed-price product revenue outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
use_cases.available_tables_listing: Only the primary tables are available: samples.nyctaxi.trips
use_cases.technique_implementation_guidance:
Method: driver analysis with a regularised linear or generalised linear model (statsmodels) of the KPI on candidate drivers; report each driver's effect size with a confidence interval and p-value, and check multicollinearity (VIF) before interpreting coefficients.
Baseline: the KPI's prior-period or overall level (a model with no drivers).
Accept: every reported driver carries an effect size and a Benjamini-Hochberg corrected significance; non-significant drivers are reported as Monitor only.
If data is insufficient: groups below the minimum rows or fewer than two periods stop the run at the readiness gate.
use_cases.genie_instruction:
## 1. Decision and Owner

This notebook changes how upfront fares are set: instead of relying on post-trip meter totals, it quantifies which route and timing drivers move `samples.nyctaxi.trips.fare_amount` so the Head of Product Pricing can ground quote-based pricing in observed effect sizes. The decision owner is the Head of Product Pricing (sponsored by the Chief Revenue Officer), and because this is a family F single run, the findings are recomputed from the data on every run (cadence: not assessed in the DECISION BLOCK). The KPI is `fare_amount`; the business priority is Increase Revenue, so the direction that matters is understanding and protecting realized fare level per unit of distance and timing. The ranked output of drivers, each with an effect size and corrected significance, goes to the Head of Product Pricing.

## 2. Data Plan

There is one table, `samples.nyctaxi.trips`, serving as the event fact table (data category TRANSACTIONAL); there is no entity or reference table and no foreign key relationship, so there is no join. The entity key for a finding is the driver dimension (corridor and timing buckets) engineered below, not a row-level primary key, because the use case explains variation in `fare_amount` across groups. The time column is `samples.nyctaxi.trips.tpep_pickup_datetime`; the as-of rule uses only trips with `tpep_pickup_datetime` strictly before `ctx["as_of_date"]`. This is a regression driver analysis, not a supervised event-prediction task, so there is no event window or open-case exclusion; the target `fare_amount` is observed per completed trip row. Population filters: keep rows where `fare_amount` is not null and `fare_amount > 0`, `trip_distance` is not null and `trip_distance > 0`, and `pickup_zip` and `dropoff_zip` are both not null (invalid, zero or negative fares and distances are degenerate records that would distort effect sizes).

## 3. Readiness Checks

- `row_count`: count the rows of `samples.nyctaxi.trips` that pass the population filters in Section 2 and have `tpep_pickup_datetime` strictly before `ctx["as_of_date"]`; threshold >= 1.
- `join_coverage`: this use case reads one table (`samples.nyctaxi.trips`) with no join path, so return 1.0; threshold >= 0.8.
- `smallest_group_rows`: form the corridor-by-timing groups used in the analysis (for example pickup/dropoff zip corridor crossed with hour-of-day bucket and day-of-week derived from `tpep_pickup_datetime`), count rows per group over the filtered rows, and return the minimum group count; threshold >= 30. Groups below 30 rows are reported as Monitor only, not stopped individually, but the smallest group drives this readiness value.
- `periods`: count the distinct time periods (distinct calendar dates, or distinct months if dates are too few) present in `tpep_pickup_datetime` over the filtered rows; threshold >= 2.

## 4. Slot Tasks

`measure_readiness(ctx)` (reads `samples.nyctaxi.trips`): run the four computations in Section 3 against the filtered, as-of rows and return the dict `{'row_count', 'join_coverage', 'smallest_group_rows', 'periods'}` with those exact keys; return 1.0 for `join_coverage` since there is one table.

`build_inputs(ctx)` (reads `samples.nyctaxi.trips`): return a Spark DataFrame of trips passing the Section 2 filters with `tpep_pickup_datetime` strictly before `ctx["as_of_date"]` (the leakage guard: no row at or after the as-of date enters any feature or target). Engineer and keep: `fare_amount` (target), `trip_distance`, a corridor label from `pickup_zip` and `dropoff_zip`, `hour_of_day` and `day_of_week` derived from `tpep_pickup_datetime`, and a weekend flag. Do not include `tpep_dropoff_datetime` or any quantity known only after the trip completes.

`analyze(ctx, inputs)` (consumes the DataFrame from `build_inputs`): fit the regression of `fare_amount` on the engineered drivers (Section 5) and return a pandas DataFrame with one row per driver finding and exactly these columns: `entity_id` (the finding key, for example the driver name), `segment_or_item` (the group or dimension level, for example a corridor or hour bucket), `value` (the effect size on `fare_amount` against the baseline), `p_value`, and `n` (rows behind the finding). Inspire applies the Benjamini-Hochberg correction.

## 5. Method and Baseline

Use a regularised linear regression (Ridge, alpha tuned by cross-validation) of `fare_amount` on `trip_distance`, corridor, hour-of-day and day-of-week features, implemented with statsmodels/scikit-learn so each driver carries an effect size, a confidence interval and a p-value; this is the simplest method that can beat the baseline, which is the overall mean of `fare_amount` (a model with no drivers). Check multicollinearity with VIF before interpreting coefficients and drop or combine collinear features so corridor and distance effects are separable. Acceptance in plain words: every reported driver must carry an effect size and must pass Benjamini-Hochberg corrected significance at fdr_alpha = 0.05, and drivers that are not significant after correction are reported as Monitor only. Risk handling: seasonality and time-of-day are modeled explicitly through the hour and day-of-week features; sparse corridors below 30 rows are reported as Monitor only; there is no class imbalance (continuous target) and no text input, so no AI function is called in these slots (Inspire's explanation and summary cells call `ai_query` on the top rows).

## 6. Output Mapping

Map `entity_label` to the driver finding key (`entity_id`), that is the named route or timing driver. `value` is the effect size of that driver on `fare_amount` against the overall-mean baseline, expressed in the units of `fare_amount` per unit of the driver (for example dollars per mile of `trip_distance`, or dollar shift for a corridor or hour bucket relative to baseline); VALUE_TYPE is 'effect size'. `segment_or_item` holds the group or dimension level the finding belongs to (for example the specific corridor or hour-of-day bucket). Each row's top reasons are derived from the model's signed coefficient contributions, not from an LLM. Set `data_quality_flag` to something other than ok when the finding's group has fewer than 30 rows (sparse, Monitor only) or when its driver showed high VIF before interpretation. Priority tiers and recommended actions are assigned by Inspire's rule-based writer; do not ask Genie Code or an LLM to set them.

## 7. Definition of Done

- Every GENIE SLOT (`measure_readiness`, `build_inputs`, `analyze`, and the `OUTPUT_COLUMNS`/`VALUE_TYPE` mapping) is filled, keeping its function names, arguments and return columns.
- The notebook ran top to bottom in this session with run controls set to Here, and then as the tagged job.
- The contract-check cell (the last cell) printed PASSED.
- No Inspire cell was edited, no threshold was changed in code, the notebook was not renamed, and no job was created or deleted; only the GENIE SLOT cells (and, if needed, one pinned `%pip install name==version` line) were touched.
- Only `samples.nyctaxi.trips` columns listed under TABLES were cited, with fully qualified table names and no invented numbers.
- STOP RULE: if the readiness gate raises `InspireReadinessStop` (or `InspireNoChampion`/`InspireRejected`), stop and show the user the plain message the gate printed; do not lower thresholds, fabricate data, drop a check, switch tables or edit the gate to force a pass.

use_cases.Name: Segment Pickup Zones by Trip Economics with Pricing Zone Strategy
use_cases.usecase: Segment Pickup Zones to Improve Margins
use_cases.Statement: Pickup zones differ widely in trip distance, fare levels and trip duration, but without data-driven grouping the pricing team treats all zones uniformly, leaving margin opportunities on the table. Zone-level economics are hidden in raw `fare_amount` and `trip_distance` distributions.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates per-zone features from `pickup_zip`, `fare_amount`, `trip_distance` and durations from `tpep_pickup_datetime`/`tpep_dropoff_datetime`, runs K-Means clustering to group zones into economic segments, then uses ai_query to recommend a pricing posture per segment.
use_cases.Business Value: The Pricing Manager assigns a differentiated pricing posture per zone segment, aiming to increase average `fare_amount` per trip in under-monetized zones and protect volume in price-sensitive ones [ESTIMATE: depends on `fare_amount`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: pickup_zip, fare_amount, trip_distance, tpep_pickup_datetime, tpep_dropoff_datetime. Compute per-zone averages and dispersion of fare, distance, fare-per-mile and duration, standardize features, run K-Means (k selected by silhouette), then use ai_query to label each cluster and recommend a pricing strategy.
use_cases.Justification: Zone economic segmentation directly supports differentiated pricing posture that lifts average fare in under-monetized zones, moving a revenue line computable from per-zone fare_amount aggregates.
use_cases.Quality Summary: Per-zone features from `pickup_zip`, `fare_amount`, `trip_distance` and durations (`tpep_pickup_datetime`/`tpep_dropoff_datetime`) are aggregated into fare-per-mile, dispersion and avg-duration metrics, standardized, then clustered with K-Means (k by silhouette) to produce zone economic segments. ai_query maps segments to a pricing posture, delivering the per-zone fare-increase outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
use_cases.available_tables_listing: Only the primary tables are available: samples.nyctaxi.trips
use_cases.technique_implementation_guidance:
Method: K-Means or a Gaussian mixture inside a scikit-learn Pipeline with imputation and scaling, choosing the number of segments by silhouette. Use only models that can assign new entities, so segment IDs stay stable between runs.
Baseline: quantile tiers on the most variable feature.
Accept: silhouette, the smallest segment share and bootstrap stability (adjusted Rand index) meet the thresholds.
If data is insufficient: too few entities for the number of segments or fewer than three usable numeric features stop the run at the readiness gate.
use_cases.genie_instruction:
## 1. Decision and Owner

This notebook changes how the Pricing team sets a pricing posture per pickup zone: instead of treating all zones uniformly, it groups pickup zones into stable economic segments so a differentiated posture can be assigned to each. The decision owner is the Head of Pricing (beneficiary), sponsored by the Chief Revenue Officer; cadence is not assessed, so follow the run modes (Auto retrains when the champion is missing, older than 30 days, or input drift PSI reaches 0.25). The business priority is Increase Revenue, so a better outcome is a higher average `samples.nyctaxi.trips.fare_amount` per trip in under-monetized zones while protecting volume in price-sensitive ones [ESTIMATE: depends on `samples.nyctaxi.trips.fare_amount`]. The ranked segment output goes to the Head of Pricing.

## 2. Data Plan

There is one table, `samples.nyctaxi.trips`, used as event facts (TRANSACTIONAL trip records). There is no join: this is a single-table use case, so join coverage is 1.0 by definition and no reference or entity table is read. The entity is the pickup zone: the entity key is `samples.nyctaxi.trips.pickup_zip`. The time column is `samples.nyctaxi.trips.tpep_pickup_datetime`. As-of rule: every feature for an as-of date is computed only from trips whose `samples.nyctaxi.trips.tpep_pickup_datetime` is strictly before `ctx["as_of_date"]`. This is a clustering (unsupervised) use case, so there is no outcome event or label window. Population filters that define the zones the decision acts on: keep rows where `samples.nyctaxi.trips.pickup_zip` is not null, `samples.nyctaxi.trips.fare_amount` is non-null and greater than 0, `samples.nyctaxi.trips.trip_distance` is non-null and greater than 0, and `samples.nyctaxi.trips.tpep_dropoff_datetime` is greater than `samples.nyctaxi.trips.tpep_pickup_datetime` so durations are positive.

## 3. Readiness Checks

- `row_count`: count trips in `samples.nyctaxi.trips` with `tpep_pickup_datetime` strictly before `ctx["as_of_date"]` that pass the population filters in Section 2.
- `join_coverage`: single-table use case, so return 1.0.
- `entities`: count distinct `samples.nyctaxi.trips.pickup_zip` among the filtered rows (each distinct zip is one entity to be clustered).
- `k`: the number of candidate segments the method will try to assign; set it to the maximum candidate k that `fit_candidates` evaluates, so the gate can enforce entities >= 10 x k.
- `numeric_features`: count the per-zone numeric features `build_inputs` produces (must be >= 3); report the actual count built from fare, distance, fare-per-mile and duration aggregates.

## 4. Slot Tasks

`measure_readiness(ctx)` reads only `samples.nyctaxi.trips`. Apply the Section 2 as-of and population filters, then return the dict with `row_count` (filtered trip count), `join_coverage` = 1.0, `entities` (distinct `pickup_zip`), `k` (the largest candidate segment count), and `numeric_features` (count of per-zone numeric features it will build, >= 3).

`build_inputs(ctx, as_of_date)` reads only `samples.nyctaxi.trips`. Leakage guard: filter to `tpep_pickup_datetime < as_of_date` strictly before any aggregation, then apply the Section 2 filters. Aggregate per `pickup_zip` to one row per zone with these numeric features (at least three): mean and standard deviation of `fare_amount`, mean of `trip_distance`, mean fare-per-mile (`fare_amount` / `trip_distance`), and mean trip duration in minutes from (`tpep_dropoff_datetime` minus `tpep_pickup_datetime`). Return a Spark DataFrame with `entity_id` set to `pickup_zip` cast to string, the numeric feature columns, and an optional text column `entity_label` holding the zip code as text.

`fit_candidates(ctx, X, seed)` builds a scikit-learn Pipeline of SimpleImputer then StandardScaler then KMeans with `random_state=seed`, one pipeline per candidate k (for example k from 2 to a cap such that entities >= 10 x k). Return `{name: fitted_pipeline}` keyed by k. `predict(ctx, model, X)` returns `model.predict(X)`, one integer segment per row. `explanation_inputs` returns None so Inspire's rule-based reasons are used.

`output_column_map` slot: map `value` to the per-zone mean `fare_amount` feature column (the KPI measure that ranks zones inside each segment); keep `entity_label` mapped to `entity_label`.

## 5. Method and Baseline

Candidate method: K-Means inside a scikit-learn Pipeline (SimpleImputer, StandardScaler, KMeans), choosing the number of segments by silhouette across the candidate k values. This is the simplest assignable model that keeps segment IDs stable between runs. Baseline Inspire fits: quantile tiers on the most variable feature (the per-zone mean `fare_amount` dispersion). Acceptance in plain words: a candidate is promoted to champion only when its silhouette is at least 0.15, its smallest segment holds at least 0.03 of the zones, and its bootstrap adjusted Rand index is at least 0.6. Data risks: sparse entities are controlled by the readiness rule entities >= 10 x k and by capping candidate k; standardization in the pipeline handles the different scales of fare, distance and duration; the imputer handles any missing feature values; seasonality is not modeled because features are long-run per-zone aggregates and no outcome window exists. Inspire's explanation and summary cells call `ai_query` on the top rows to label each segment and recommend a pricing posture; the slots add no other AI calls, and the response is plain text (a short segment label and a pricing-posture recommendation sentence).

## 6. Output Mapping

Map `entity_label` to the `entity_label` column (the pickup zip as text). `value` is the per-zone mean `fare_amount`, in US dollars per trip, used to rank zones inside each segment. `segment_or_item` holds the segment number returned by `predict`. Each row's top reasons come from Inspire's rule-based reasons (`explanation_inputs` returns None), derived from how the zone's features compare to its segment centroid (for example above-average fare-per-mile or longer-than-average duration). Set `data_quality_flag` to something other than ok when a zone's feature count behind the aggregates is thin (very few underlying trips) or when a required feature was imputed rather than observed. Priority tiers and recommended actions are set by Inspire's rule-based writer; do not ask Genie Code or an LLM to assign them.

## 7. Definition of Done

- Every GENIE SLOT (`measure_readiness`, `build_inputs`, `fit_candidates`, `predict`, `explanation_inputs`, and the `OUTPUT_COLUMNS` mapping) is filled with its function names, arguments and return columns unchanged.
- The notebook ran top to bottom in this session with run controls set to Here, and then ran as the tagged job.
- The contract-check cell (the last cell) printed PASSED.
- No Inspire cell was edited, no threshold was changed in code, the notebook was not renamed, and no job was created or deleted.
- STOP RULE: if the readiness gate raises `InspireReadinessStop`, `InspireNoChampion`, or `InspireRejected`, Genie Code must STOP, show the user the plain message the gate printed, and must not lower thresholds, fabricate data, drop a check, switch tables, or edit the gate to force a pass.

use_cases.Name: Identify Unprofitable Long-Distance Trips with Route Pricing Corrections
use_cases.usecase: Identify Low-yield Trips to Protect Margins
use_cases.Statement: Some long-distance trips return low `fare_amount` relative to `trip_distance` and elapsed duration, dragging down effective yield, but these low-yield trips are not separated from healthy ones in reporting. Uncorrected, they erode margin on every repeat.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code derives fare-per-mile and fare-per-minute from `fare_amount`, `trip_distance`, `tpep_pickup_datetime` and `tpep_dropoff_datetime`, trains a Random Forest classifier to label trips as low-yield versus healthy using corridor features from `pickup_zip`/`dropoff_zip`, then uses ai_query to recommend route-level pricing corrections.
use_cases.Business Value: The Yield Management Analyst targets corridors generating recurring low-yield trips, aiming to raise effective fare-per-mile and reduce the share of trips classified as low-yield [ESTIMATE: depends on `fare_amount`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: fare_amount, trip_distance, tpep_pickup_datetime, tpep_dropoff_datetime, pickup_zip, dropoff_zip. Derive fare-per-mile and fare-per-minute, define a yield threshold label, train a Random Forest classifier on distance, duration and corridor features, then use ai_query to recommend corridor-level pricing corrections for low-yield classes.
use_cases.Justification: Labeling low-yield corridors feeds route pricing corrections that lift effective fare-per-mile, directly moving yield, a revenue/margin line computable from fare_amount and trip_distance.
use_cases.Quality Summary: Yield signal from `fare_amount`, `trip_distance` and duration (`tpep_pickup_datetime`/`tpep_dropoff_datetime`) yields fare-per-mile and fare-per-minute; a Random Forest classifier using `pickup_zip`/`dropoff_zip` corridor features labels trips low-yield vs healthy, producing a low_yield_share KPI per corridor. ai_query recommends corridor pricing corrections, delivering the yield-improvement outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
use_cases.available_tables_listing: Only the primary tables are available: samples.nyctaxi.trips
use_cases.technique_implementation_guidance:
Method: a scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingClassifier or a regularised logistic regression on as-of features, with class weights for imbalance; frame the outcome as an event per the outcome definition.
Baseline: the class rate plus a balanced logistic regression on the strongest signals.
Accept: out-of-time AUC and PR-AUC meet the thresholds and AUC beats the baseline by the minimum gain, measured on the most recent closed outcome window (time-aware split, never a random split across time).
If data is insufficient: too few positives, an extreme class rate or fewer than two closed outcome windows stop the run at the readiness gate.
use_cases.genie_instruction:
## 1. Decision and Owner

This notebook changes which long-distance corridors a Yield Management Analyst targets for route-level pricing corrections by separating low-yield trips from healthy ones that current reporting lumps together. The decision owner is the Yield Management Analyst, with the Chief Financial Officer as sponsor; cadence is not assessed in the DECISION BLOCK, so treat it as periodic batch scoring driven by the run-mode controls. The KPI is effective fare-per-mile and the share of trips classified as low-yield: better means raising effective fare-per-mile and reducing the low-yield share [ESTIMATE: depends on `samples.nyctaxi.trips.fare_amount`]. The ranked output of flagged low-yield trips, with corridor-level pricing-correction suggestions, goes to the Yield Management Analyst.

## 2. Data Plan

There is one table, `samples.nyctaxi.trips`, in the role of event facts; it is also the entity source. There is no join (one table), so the join path is empty and join coverage is 1.0. The entity is a single trip: since the table has no trip id, build a deterministic entity key by hashing `trips.tpep_pickup_datetime`, `trips.tpep_dropoff_datetime`, `trips.pickup_zip`, `trips.dropoff_zip` and `trips.trip_distance` into one stable string so the same trip always maps to the same key. The time column is `trips.tpep_pickup_datetime`; derive `as_of_date` as the date of pickup. As-of rule: every feature for an as_of_date uses only trip attributes known at pickup time (distance, pickup and dropoff zip, pickup hour, day of week); the fare-derived outcome is used only to build the label, never as a feature.

Outcome rule (classification): the event is "trip is low-yield". Derive duration in minutes from the two timestamps and compute fare-per-mile and fare-per-minute, then label the event using a within-sample yield threshold on long-distance trips:

```python
# duration_min = (tpep_dropoff_datetime - tpep_pickup_datetime) in minutes
# fpm = fare_amount / trip_distance ; fppm = fare_amount / duration_min
# long_distance = trip_distance >= p75(trip_distance over the population)
# yield_cut = p25(fpm over long_distance trips)
# label = 1 when long_distance AND fpm <= yield_cut, else 0
```

Because the outcome is known at trip completion, there are no open cases to exclude for training; for scoring, "still open" means the most recent trips whose outcome window has not yet closed under OUTCOME_WINDOW_DAYS. Population filters: keep only rows with `trip_distance` greater than 0, `fare_amount` greater than 0, positive derived duration, and non-null `pickup_zip` and `dropoff_zip`; the decision acts on long-distance trips only, but readiness and the label are computed over this cleaned population so the model learns the healthy-versus-low-yield boundary.

## 3. Readiness Checks

- `row_count`: count rows in `samples.nyctaxi.trips` after the population filters (positive `trip_distance`, positive `fare_amount`, positive derived duration, non-null `pickup_zip` and `dropoff_zip`) with `tpep_pickup_datetime` on or before ctx["as_of_date"].
- `join_coverage`: single table, so return 1.0.
- `outcome_derivable`: True when `fare_amount`, `trip_distance`, both timestamps, `pickup_zip` and `dropoff_zip` are present and the yield threshold and label can be computed on at least one closed window; else False.
- `positives`: count of rows whose derived label equals 1 (long-distance trips at or below the yield cut) over the filtered population.
- `class_rate`: positives divided by `row_count`, the share of low-yield trips.
- `outcome_windows`: count the distinct closed outcome windows of length OUTCOME_WINDOW_DAYS between the minimum and maximum `tpep_pickup_datetime` in the filtered population.

## 4. Slot Tasks

`measure_readiness(ctx)` reads `samples.nyctaxi.trips`. Apply the population filters, derive duration, fare-per-mile and the yield threshold, then compute and return the dict with `row_count`, `join_coverage` (1.0), `outcome_derivable`, `positives`, `class_rate` and `outcome_windows` exactly as described in section 3.

`build_inputs(ctx, as_of_dates, scoring=False)` reads `samples.nyctaxi.trips` (ctx["source_tables"] when training, ctx["scoring_tables"] when scoring). Set `OUTCOME_WINDOW_DAYS` to 1 (yield is known at trip completion, same-day). Apply population filters, build the hashed `entity_id`, set `as_of_date` to the pickup date, and emit numeric features observed strictly before outcome resolution: `trip_distance`, derived duration in minutes, pickup hour, pickup day of week, and corridor identity encoded from `pickup_zip` and `dropoff_zip` (for example target-free frequency or a combined corridor code). Do not include `fare_amount`, fare-per-mile or fare-per-minute as features (leakage guard). Add a text column `entity_label` as a readable corridor string like "pickup_zip->dropoff_zip". Return entity_id, as_of_date (DATE), the numeric feature columns and entity_label, one row per trip per date; with scoring=True return only trips whose outcome window is still open on ctx["as_of_date"].

`build_label(ctx, as_of_dates)` reads `samples.nyctaxi.trips`. Recompute the yield threshold and the long-distance cut over the same filtered population, then return entity_id, as_of_date and label (1 when long-distance and fare-per-mile at or below the yield cut within OUTCOME_WINDOW_DAYS after as_of_date, else 0).

`fit_candidates(ctx, X_train, y_train)` trains on the features from `build_inputs`; set `BASELINE_FEATURES` to the strongest signals (`trip_distance`, duration, corridor code). Return a dict with one or two fitted scikit-learn estimators (see section 5). `predict(ctx, model, X)` returns one probability of the low-yield outcome per row. `explanation_inputs` returns None to use Inspire's rule-based reasons.

## 5. Method and Baseline

Candidate: a scikit-learn `RandomForestClassifier` with `class_weight="balanced"` (the use-case technique), optionally a `HistGradientBoostingClassifier` as a second candidate; keep it to one or two, no deep learning. Inspire's baseline is the class rate plus a balanced logistic regression on `BASELINE_FEATURES`. Acceptance: out-of-time AUC at least 0.60, PR-AUC at least 1.5 times the class rate, and AUC at least 0.02 above the baseline, measured on the most recent closed outcome window with a time-aware split (never a random split across time). Handle risks: use `class_weight="balanced"` for class imbalance since low-yield is the minority; split by time to respect seasonality and avoid leaking future periods; stop at the readiness gate if there are fewer than 200 positives, an extreme class rate, or fewer than two closed windows; mitigate sparse corridors by using a frequency or combined-code encoding of `pickup_zip`/`dropoff_zip` rather than high-cardinality one-hot. For the pricing-correction text, Inspire's explanation and summary cells call `ai_query` on the top rows; the slots add no other AI calls, and the response is short plain-text corridor pricing recommendations.

## 6. Output Mapping

Map `entity_label` to the corridor string "pickup_zip->dropoff_zip" built in `build_inputs`. `VALUE_TYPE` is 'probability', so `value` is the predicted probability that the trip is low-yield (unitless, 0 to 1). `segment_or_item` carries the corridor identity (the `pickup_zip`/`dropoff_zip` pair) so the analyst can aggregate recurring low-yield corridors. Each row's top reasons come from Inspire's rule-based reasons (`explanation_inputs` returns None), surfacing the most unusual feature values such as long `trip_distance` with short duration or a low-yield corridor code. Set `data_quality_flag` to something other than ok when inputs needed for the label or features are missing or implausible: non-positive `trip_distance` or `fare_amount`, non-positive derived duration, or null `pickup_zip`/`dropoff_zip`. Priority tiers and recommended actions are assigned by Inspire's writer; do not ask Genie Code or an LLM to set them.

use_cases.genie_instruction:
## 1. Decision and Owner

This notebook changes how the Head of Fleet Operations decides where to pre-position vehicles before each shift, replacing idle-guesswork with a forward-looking hourly trip-demand forecast per pickup zone. The decision owner is the Head of Fleet Operations (sponsored by the Chief Operating Officer); the cadence is per shift, as stated in the use case (the DECISION BLOCK did not formally assess cadence, so treat it as shift-level). The KPI is served-trip volume per pickup zone (count of rows per `pickup_zip` over an hourly bucket), where higher forecasted demand in a zone signals where to send vehicles; better means more accurately anticipating high-demand zones so fewer vehicles sit idle. The ranked forecast output goes to the Head of Fleet Operations for shift-level pre-positioning.

## 2. Data Plan

There is one table, `samples.nyctaxi.trips`, serving as the event-fact table; it contains no entity or reference table and no foreign keys, so there is no join and join coverage is defined as 1.0. The entity key is `samples.nyctaxi.trips.pickup_zip` (the series key, one series per pickup zone). The time column is `samples.nyctaxi.trips.tpep_pickup_datetime`. This is a forecasting use case, not supervised classification, so there is no outcome label or open-case exclusion; the modeled quantity is the count of trip rows per `pickup_zip` per time bucket. The as-of rule: every series stops at `ctx["as_of_date"]` and uses only rows where `tpep_pickup_datetime` falls strictly before the forecast origin, so no future period informs a fit. Population filter: keep rows with a non-null `pickup_zip` and a non-null `tpep_pickup_datetime`; restrict to zones with enough history to backtest (see Slot Tasks), dropping ultra-sparse zones that cannot support at least two seasonal cycles.

## 3. Readiness Checks

- `row_count`: count all rows in `samples.nyctaxi.trips` with non-null `tpep_pickup_datetime` and non-null `pickup_zip` observed on or before `ctx["as_of_date"]`; must be >= 1.
- `join_coverage`: this use case reads one table with no join path, so return 1.0 (meets the >= 0.8 threshold).
- `seasonal_cycles`: compute the span from the earliest to the latest `tpep_pickup_datetime` (filtered as above) in units of SEASON_LENGTH periods, that is (number of distinct hourly periods covered) divided by SEASON_LENGTH; must be >= 2. Use the overall history span, not per-zone, so a weak zone does not block the whole run.
- `staleness_cadences`: compute the gap between the latest `tpep_pickup_datetime` and `ctx["as_of_date"]` measured in periods (hours), then divide by SEASON_LENGTH to express it in cadences; must be <= 2.
- `missing_period_rate`: over the full history span, build the complete grid of expected hourly periods and compute the share of expected periods that have zero trips (aggregated across the retained high-volume zones); must be <= 0.2.

## 4. Slot Tasks

**measure_readiness (slot 3a)** reads only `samples.nyctaxi.trips`. Filter to non-null `pickup_zip` and `tpep_pickup_datetime` at or before `ctx["as_of_date"]`, truncate `tpep_pickup_datetime` to the hour, and compute the five keys exactly as in Section 3. Return the dict with keys `row_count`, `join_coverage` (set to 1.0), `seasonal_cycles`, `staleness_cadences`, `missing_period_rate`.

**build_inputs (slot 4)** reads only `samples.nyctaxi.trips`. Set SEASON_LENGTH to 24 (24 hourly periods make one daily season of hour-of-day demand) and HORIZON to 24 (one shift-forward day of hourly buckets; adjust only if the data span cannot support 24, but keep it a whole number of hours). Aggregate: truncate `tpep_pickup_datetime` to the hour, group by `pickup_zip` and that hourly bucket, count rows. Return a Spark DataFrame with `entity_id` (= `pickup_zip`), `period` (the hourly bucket as a timestamp/DATE-like period, one row per zone per period up to `ctx["as_of_date"]`), and `value` (the hourly trip count, with explicit zeros for hours in the covered span that had no trips, so gaps are not silently dropped). Leakage guard: include only periods strictly before the forecast origin derived from `ctx["as_of_date"]`; never let a period at or after the origin enter history. Retain only high-volume zones that have at least two full seasonal cycles of history so each series can be backtested.

**forecast (slot 5)** takes the pandas `history` (`entity_id`, `period`, `value`) and `horizon`. For each `entity_id`, refit on the full given history every call (never register or persist a model), fit the chosen per-series model, and generate the next `horizon` hourly periods after that series' last period. Return a pandas DataFrame with columns `entity_id`, `period`, `forecast`. If a series is too short or the fit fails, fall back to the seasonal naive value (the count one season earlier) for that series.

**OUTPUT_COLUMNS mapping (slot 8a)** keeps the Inspire-prefilled standard columns and sets `entity_label` to the pickup-zone identifier; VALUE_TYPE stays `forecast`.

## 5. Method and Baseline

Candidate method: one gradient-boosted regressor (for example LightGBM or scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingRegressor) trained across all zones at once with calendar and lag features (hour-of-day, day-of-week, and lag/rolling features over `value`), which is simpler to operate than one model per zone and handles sparse zones by sharing signal; if that underperforms, a per-series statsmodels ExponentialSmoothing or SARIMAX with a seasonal period of SEASON_LENGTH is the fallback. No deep learning. The baseline Inspire fits is the seasonal naive forecast (the value one season, 24 hours, earlier). Acceptance in plain words: a rolling-origin backtest with at least 3 folds must give MASE below 1.0 against the seasonal naive forecast; if it does not, the notebook publishes the seasonal naive forecast, flagged, instead of the candidate. Data risks: strong daily seasonality is captured by SEASON_LENGTH = 24 and hour-of-day features; missing periods are filled with explicit zeros in build_inputs and bounded by the readiness `missing_period_rate` check; sparse zones are either pooled into the single cross-series model or dropped if below two seasonal cycles. No AI function is called in these slots; Inspire's own explanation and summary cells call `ai_query` on the top rows to turn the per-zone forecast into shift-level pre-positioning language.

## 6. Output Mapping

Map `entity_label` to the pickup zone (`pickup_zip`). The `value` column holds the forecasted hourly trip count per zone per future period (unit: trips per hour), with VALUE_TYPE `forecast`. Put the forecast period (the future hourly bucket, or the shift it rolls up to) in `segment_or_item` so each row is identified by zone and time. Each row's top reasons are derived from the model's drivers in plain terms (for example recent same-hour demand lag and day-of-week pattern) rather than from any LLM. Set `data_quality_flag` to something other than ok when the zone was published on the seasonal naive fallback because its MASE did not beat the baseline, when a zone had below two seasonal cycles of history, or when its `missing_period_rate` within the series was elevated; otherwise ok. Priority tiers and recommended actions are assigned by Inspire's rule-based writer; do not ask Genie Code or an LLM to set them.

## 7. Definition of Done

- All four GENIE SLOTs (3a readiness queries, 4 series, 5 forecaster, 8a output mapping) are filled with their original function names, arguments and return columns, and SEASON_LENGTH and HORIZON are set.
- The notebook ran top to bottom in this session with run controls set to Here, and then ran as the tagged job, with no Inspire cell edited, no notebook rename, and no job created or deleted.
- Only slot cells (and, if truly needed, one pinned `%pip install name==version` line in the Pinned packages cell) were changed.
- The final contract-check cell printed PASSED.
- No invented numbers were introduced and only fully qualified table names were used, with no serverless-forbidden APIs.
- STOP RULE: if the readiness gate raises `InspireReadinessStop` (or `InspireNoChampion` / `InspireRejected`), Genie Code must stop, show the user the plain message the gate printed, and must not lower thresholds, fabricate data, drop a check, switch tables or edit the gate to force a pass.

domains.summary:
Risk management protects the integrity of Samples nyctaxi's revenue and service promise, ensuring that fares are billed correctly and trips meet quality expectations. This domain safeguards the trust that underpins every transaction between riders, drivers, and the platform.

Detect Fare Irregularities to Protect Revenue equips the Revenue Assurance Analyst with a daily queue of flagged trips to recover revenue tied to under-billed trips, closing leakage before it compounds. Detect Slow Trips to Protect Revenue gives the Service Quality Lead a ranked alert queue of abnormally slow trips, targeting reductions in excess duration-per-trip and improving the rider experience. With Databricks Genie Code, anomaly detection becomes faster to deploy and easier to investigate, transforming risk from a reactive cost center into a proactive guardian of revenue and quality.

use_cases.genie_instruction:
## 1. Decision and Owner

This notebook changes which trips enter the daily revenue-assurance investigation queue, flagging trips where `fare_amount` is inconsistent with `trip_distance` and derived trip duration so meter errors, fare manipulation and data-entry faults can be reviewed. The decision owner is the Revenue Assurance Analyst, who works the ranked queue; the Chief Financial Officer sponsors the effort. Cadence, KPI and value tier are not assessed in the DECISION BLOCK, so treat the cadence as a per-run queue aimed at reducing the count of anomalous `fare_amount` values [ESTIMATE: depends on `fare_amount`], with "better" meaning more true irregularities surfaced within the review budget. The ranked output goes to the Revenue Assurance Analyst as the investigation queue.

## 2. Data Plan

Only `samples.nyctaxi.trips` is in scope; it is the event-fact table and the sole source, so there is no join and join coverage is 1.0 by definition. The entity is one trip; `samples.nyctaxi.trips` has no natural key, so build a deterministic entity key by hashing the tuple (`trips.tpep_pickup_datetime`, `trips.tpep_dropoff_datetime`, `trips.pickup_zip`, `trips.dropoff_zip`, `trips.trip_distance`, `trips.fare_amount`) so the same trip row maps to a stable id across runs. The time column is `trips.tpep_pickup_datetime`. As-of rule: the reference window is strictly before `ctx["as_of_date"]`; the current window is on or after it. This is an unsupervised anomaly use case, so there is no outcome event or label rule to state. Population filters that define the decision set: keep rows where `trips.fare_amount` and `trips.trip_distance` are non-null, `trips.trip_distance` > 0, `trips.fare_amount` > 0, and derived duration (`trips.tpep_dropoff_datetime` minus `trips.tpep_pickup_datetime`) is strictly positive, because fare-per-mile and fare-per-minute are undefined otherwise.

## 3. Data Readiness Checks

- `row_count`: count all rows of `samples.nyctaxi.trips` after the population filters in section 2, over the full table as of `ctx["as_of_date"]`; must be >= 1.
- `join_coverage`: single table, no join, so return 1.0; must be >= 0.8.
- `reference_rows`: count filtered rows of `samples.nyctaxi.trips` with `trips.tpep_pickup_datetime` strictly before `ctx["as_of_date"]` (the reference window); must be >= 1000.
- `key_signal_null_rate`: over all rows of `samples.nyctaxi.trips` as of `ctx["as_of_date"]`, the share of rows where `trips.fare_amount`, `trips.trip_distance`, `trips.tpep_pickup_datetime` or `trips.tpep_dropoff_datetime` is null, or where `trips.trip_distance` <= 0 or the derived duration is <= 0; must be <= 0.2.

## 4. Slot Tasks

`measure_readiness(ctx)` reads only `samples.nyctaxi.trips`. Compute the four keys exactly as in section 3 (row_count, join_coverage=1.0, reference_rows, key_signal_null_rate) and return them in one dict. All counts respect the as-of date through `trips.tpep_pickup_datetime`.

`build_inputs(ctx, window)` reads only `samples.nyctaxi.trips`. Apply the section 2 filters. For window "reference" keep rows with `trips.tpep_pickup_datetime` strictly before `ctx["as_of_date"]`; for "current" keep rows on or after it. This split is the leakage guard: the reference window that defines normal never includes current-window rows. Derive `trip_duration_minutes` = (`trips.tpep_dropoff_datetime` minus `trips.tpep_pickup_datetime`) in minutes, `fare_per_mile` = `trips.fare_amount` / `trips.trip_distance`, and `fare_per_minute` = `trips.fare_amount` / `trip_duration_minutes`. Return a Spark DataFrame with columns: `entity_id` (the stable hash from section 2), the numeric signals `fare_amount` (from `trips.fare_amount`), `trip_distance` (from `trips.trip_distance`), `trip_duration_minutes`, `fare_per_mile`, `fare_per_minute`, and an `entity_label` text column such as a concatenation of pickup zip to dropoff zip (`trips.pickup_zip`, `trips.dropoff_zip`) with the pickup timestamp.

`fit_candidates(ctx, X_reference, seed)` uses scikit-learn only. Fit `IsolationForest(contamination=0.03, random_state=seed)` on the numeric signal columns of `X_reference` and return `{"isolation_forest": model}`. Scale or clip extreme ratios only if needed; no deep learning.

`predict(ctx, model, X)` returns one anomaly score per row of `X`, higher meaning more unusual, as `-model.score_samples(X)` using the same numeric signal columns in the same order as fitting.

`explanation_inputs(ctx, model, X)` returns None so Inspire's rule-based reasons are used.

## 5. Method and Baseline

The candidate method is a single scikit-learn `IsolationForest(contamination=0.03)` on the five numeric signals (`fare_amount`, `trip_distance`, `trip_duration_minutes`, `fare_per_mile`, `fare_per_minute`), the simplest detector that can beat the baseline. The baseline Inspire fits is a robust z-score rule using median and MAD on the same signals. Acceptance in plain words: the run keeps at most 200 alerts (alerts taken at the 0.99 quantile of the anomaly score), the top alerts from two fits with different seeds must agree at least 0.6, and precision on any known cases must not fall below the baseline. Risk handling: ratios like fare-per-mile and fare-per-minute are undefined when distance or duration is zero, so the population filters in section 2 remove those rows before fitting; there is no label so class imbalance is addressed by the fixed contamination and the alert budget; seasonality and missing periods are handled by always fitting on a reference window strictly before the scored window so the detector never trains on the rows it scores. No AI function is called in the slots; Inspire's explanation and summary cells already apply `ai_query` to the top rows.

## 6. Output Mapping

Map `entity_label` to the `entity_label` column built in `build_inputs` (pickup-to-dropoff zips with pickup timestamp, from `trips.pickup_zip`, `trips.dropoff_zip`, `trips.tpep_pickup_datetime`). `VALUE_TYPE` is 'anomaly score', so `value` is the per-trip anomaly score from `predict` (unitless, higher means more unusual). `segment_or_item` identifies the trip, carrying the pickup-dropoff zip pair from `trips.pickup_zip` and `trips.dropoff_zip`. Each row's top reasons come from Inspire's rule-based reasons (explanation_inputs returns None), which describe which signals (fare_amount, trip_distance, the derived duration, fare_per_mile, fare_per_minute) deviated most. Set `data_quality_flag` to something other than ok when a row had a borderline derived value, for example a very small positive `trips.trip_distance` or duration that inflates a ratio, or when `fare_per_mile` or `fare_per_minute` is extreme enough to suggest a data-entry fault rather than a genuine fare. Priority tiers and recommended actions are assigned by Inspire's writer; do not set them in the slots or via an LLM.

## 7. Definition of Done

- All four GENIE SLOT functions are filled: `measure_readiness`, `build_inputs`, `fit_candidates` with `predict` and `explanation_inputs`, and the `OUTPUT_COLUMNS` / `VALUE_TYPE` mapping.
- Every function returns exactly the required columns and keys, and cites only `samples.nyctaxi.trips` columns listed under TABLES.
- The notebook ran top to bottom in this session with run controls set to Here, and then ran as the tagged job.
- The contract-check cell (the last cell) printed PASSED.
- No Inspire cell was edited, no threshold was changed in code, the notebook was not renamed, and no job was created or deleted; the only allowed outside-slot edit is a pinned `%pip install` line if a slot needs a missing package.
- STOP RULE: if the readiness gate raises `InspireReadinessStop` (or `InspireNoChampion` / `InspireRejected`), Genie Code stops, shows the user the plain message the gate printed, and does not lower thresholds, fabricate data, drop a check, switch tables or edit the gate to force a pass.

use_cases.Name: Detect Abnormally Slow Trips for Equivalent Routes with Service Alert Queue
use_cases.usecase: Detect Slow Trips to Protect Revenue
use_cases.Statement: Trips covering similar distances between the same pickup and dropoff zones sometimes take far longer than peers, signaling congestion, detours, or meter issues that erode trip throughput and rider trust. Flagging these outliers lets operations investigate systemic route problems.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code groups trips by `pickup_zip` and `dropoff_zip`, computes trip duration from `tpep_pickup_datetime` and `tpep_dropoff_datetime` normalized by `trip_distance`, trains an Isolation Forest on duration-per-mile and distance features to flag outlier trips, then uses ai_query to explain each flagged trip and generate an investigation alert.
use_cases.Business Value: The Service Quality Lead works a ranked alert queue of abnormally slow trips, targeting a reduction in excess duration-per-mile derived from `tpep_pickup_datetime`, `tpep_dropoff_datetime` and `trip_distance` [ESTIMATE: depends on trip_distance].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: pickup_zip, dropoff_zip, tpep_pickup_datetime, tpep_dropoff_datetime, trip_distance. Derive duration = dropoff minus pickup, compute duration-per-mile per zone pair, engineer features (duration-per-mile, distance, hour-of-day), train Isolation Forest to flag slow outliers, then use ai_query to explain flags and build an investigation alert queue.
use_cases.Strategic Goals Alignment: Enable Data-Driven Decisions, Improve Customer Experience, Boost Productivity
use_cases.Justification: Flagging slow trips per zone pair targets throughput and rider trust, an efficiency and quality KPI whose revenue effect is indirect; still a defensible always-on alert queue.
use_cases.Quality Summary: Signal from duration (`tpep_dropoff_datetime` minus `tpep_pickup_datetime`) normalized by `trip_distance` within `pickup_zip`/`dropoff_zip` peer groups; computing duration-per-mile per zone pair feeds an Isolation Forest with hour-of-day context, yielding a slowness anomaly_score per trip. Ranking flagged outliers into a service alert queue drives the throughput and route-issue investigation outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on trip_distance].
use_cases.available_tables_listing: Only the primary tables are available: samples.nyctaxi.trips
use_cases.technique_implementation_guidance:
Method: Isolation Forest, or Local Outlier Factor with novelty=True, from scikit-learn on numeric signals, fitted on a reference window that always precedes the scored window.
Baseline: a robust z-score rule (median and MAD) on the same signals.
Accept: the alerts fit the review budget, the top alerts of two fits with different seeds agree at the stability threshold, and precision on any known cases is not below the baseline.
If data is insufficient: too few reference rows or mostly missing key signals stop the run at the readiness gate; never score with a detector trained on a thin window.

domains.summary:
The Revenue domain focuses on growing and stabilizing Samples nyctaxi's top line by aligning incentives, expectations, and commercial focus with real demand patterns. It translates predictive insight into coordinated actions that drive measurable financial outcomes.

Forecast Revenue Peaks to Grow Revenue enables the Driver Incentives Manager to schedule bonus windows around forecast revenue peaks to lift total fare_amount, while Forecast Trip Duration to Improve Satisfaction helps the Customer Experience Manager set corridor-level arrival estimates that reduce the gap between promised and actual times. Identify Top Trip Corridors to Grow Revenue lets the Commercial Strategy Lead concentrate supply and promotional spend on the vital-few corridors to grow total fare revenue. Databricks Genie Code empowers these teams to forecast, test, and act with speed, turning revenue strategy into a continuous, insight-led practice.

use_cases.Name: Forecast Hourly Revenue to Anticipate Peak Earnings Windows with Driver Incentive Plan
use_cases.usecase: Forecast Revenue Peaks to Grow Revenue
use_cases.Statement: Revenue intensity concentrates in specific hourly windows, but without a forward revenue forecast the incentives team cannot time driver bonuses to the highest-yield periods, leaving peak demand under-supplied. Realized `fare_amount` per hour varies sharply.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates summed `fare_amount` into hourly buckets from `tpep_pickup_datetime`, fits an ai_forecast time-series model with hour and weekday seasonality, then uses ai_query to recommend when to deploy driver incentives for peak earnings windows.
use_cases.Business Value: The Driver Incentives Manager schedules bonus windows around forecast revenue peaks, aiming to increase total `fare_amount` captured during peak hours and lift driver availability when it matters most [ESTIMATE: depends on `fare_amount`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: tpep_pickup_datetime, fare_amount. Aggregate summed fare_amount into hourly buckets, engineer hour-of-day and weekday seasonal features, fit an ai_forecast model to project hourly revenue, then use ai_query to recommend incentive-window placement from the forecast.
use_cases.Strategic Goals Alignment: Enable Data-Driven Decisions, Increase Revenue, Boost Productivity
use_cases.Justification: Hourly revenue forecasting times driver incentives to peak windows, lifting fare captured and availability when it matters, a revenue line computable from summed fare_amount per hour.
use_cases.Quality Summary: Revenue signal from `fare_amount` summed into hourly buckets off `tpep_pickup_datetime`; engineering hour-of-day and weekday seasonal features feeds an ai_forecast model producing a projected_hourly_revenue series. ai_query places incentive windows on forecast peaks, directly serving the peak-earnings capture outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
use_cases.available_tables_listing: Only the primary tables are available: samples.nyctaxi.trips
use_cases.technique_implementation_guidance:
Method: refit on the full history every run (statsmodels exponential smoothing or SARIMAX per series, or one gradient-boosted model with calendar and lag features across series); never register per-series models. ai_forecast() runs only through a SQL warehouse, not in this notebook.
Baseline: the seasonal naive forecast (the value one season earlier).
Accept: a rolling-origin backtest with at least three folds gives MASE below 1 against the seasonal naive forecast; otherwise the notebook publishes the seasonal naive forecast, flagged.
If data is insufficient: fewer than two seasonal cycles, stale data or many missing periods stop the run at the readiness gate.

use_cases.Name: Forecast Zone Pair Trip Duration with Rider Wait Time Communication Plan
use_cases.usecase: Forecast Trip Duration to Improve Satisfaction
use_cases.Statement: Expected travel time between zone pairs shifts by hour and day, and inaccurate estimates frustrate riders and complicate dispatch promises. Forecasting duration per zone pair and time window supports reliable arrival estimates and better rider communication.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates trip duration (from `tpep_pickup_datetime` to `tpep_dropoff_datetime`) by `pickup_zip`, `dropoff_zip` and time bucket, fits a time-series forecast with calendar features from the pickup timestamp, then uses ai_query to explain duration drivers and recommend rider wait-time messaging per corridor.
use_cases.Business Value: The Customer Experience Manager sets corridor-level arrival estimates, aiming to reduce the error between promised and actual duration derived from `tpep_pickup_datetime` and `tpep_dropoff_datetime` [ESTIMATE: depends on tpep_dropoff_datetime].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: tpep_pickup_datetime, tpep_dropoff_datetime, pickup_zip, dropoff_zip. Compute trip duration, aggregate by zone pair and hourly/day-of-week bucket, fit Prophet or ai_forecast with calendar features, then use ai_query to explain duration patterns and recommend rider communication rules.
use_cases.Strategic Goals Alignment: Enable Data-Driven Decisions, Improve Customer Experience
use_cases.Justification: Zone-pair duration forecasting improves arrival estimates and rider communication, a customer-experience KPI whose revenue effect is indirect but a defensible recurring forecast.
use_cases.Quality Summary: Duration signal from `tpep_pickup_datetime` and `tpep_dropoff_datetime` aggregated by `pickup_zip`/`dropoff_zip` and hourly/day-of-week bucket; fitting Prophet or ai_forecast with calendar features produces a projected_duration per corridor-time. ai_query turns forecasts into rider wait-time messaging, serving the arrival-estimate accuracy outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on tpep_dropoff_datetime].

use_cases.Name: Reveal Revenue Concentration Across Trip Corridors with Corridor Investment Plan
use_cases.usecase: Identify Top Trip Corridors to Grow Revenue
use_cases.Statement: A small share of pickup-to-dropoff corridors likely drives a disproportionate share of total `fare_amount`, but the commercial team lacks visibility into which `pickup_zip` to `dropoff_zip` corridors concentrate revenue. Spreading investment evenly wastes effort.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code groups trips by the `pickup_zip` and `dropoff_zip` corridor pair, sums `fare_amount` and trip counts, applies a Pareto ranking to find the vital-few corridors, then uses ai_query to recommend where to concentrate driver supply and promotion.
use_cases.Business Value: The Commercial Strategy Lead focuses supply and promotional spend on the vital-few corridors, aiming to grow total `fare_amount` captured on high-yield corridors while trimming effort on long-tail routes [ESTIMATE: depends on `fare_amount`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: pickup_zip, dropoff_zip, fare_amount. Build corridor keys from pickup_zip and dropoff_zip, aggregate summed fare_amount and trip counts per corridor, compute cumulative revenue share for Pareto ranking, then use ai_query to produce a corridor investment plan from the ranked list.
use_cases.Justification: Pareto ranking of corridors by summed fare concentrates supply and promotion on the vital-few, directly moving revenue captured on high-yield corridors, computable from fare_amount by corridor.
use_cases.Quality Summary: Corridor key built from `pickup_zip` and `dropoff_zip`; aggregating SUM(`fare_amount`) and COUNT per corridor yields revenue_per_corridor, and cumulative revenue share produces a Pareto ranking identifying the vital-few corridors. ai_query turns the ranked list into a corridor investment plan, directly serving the revenue-concentration outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on fare_amount].
use_cases.available_tables_listing: Only the primary tables are available: samples.nyctaxi.trips
use_cases.technique_implementation_guidance:
Method: cumulative share of the KPI by contributor with the Gini coefficient, and a bootstrap confidence interval for the top contributors' share.
Baseline: an even split across contributors and the prior period's concentration.
Accept: every reported concentration change carries an effect size and a Benjamini-Hochberg corrected significance.
If data is insufficient: contributors below the minimum rows or fewer than two periods stop the run at the readiness gate.
